money.description: A dollar figure, or null meaning the source did not publish it. Nulls must be accounted for in not_published or lines_flagged -- see the budget schema. Stored in whole dollars unless the source states cents.

fte.description: Full-time-equivalent headcount, or null meaning the source did not publish it.

entity_ref.description: Stable internal registry slug. Deliberately independent of AOE organization IDs, which will churn as Act 170 mergers close in 2029 -- these URLs and this historical data must not. A "source/" slug names a publisher of data rather than an organization in the registry, for datasets whose publisher has no organization record of its own.

aoe_org_id.description: AOE organization ID as published by the Public Data API. Note the API spells this key `OrgID` on the organizations/supervisoryUnions/closed_organizations endpoints and `OrgId` on towns/publicSchools/unionDistricts; the sync normalizes both to this field. The pattern is deliberately permissive: this is a field we do not control, and observed values include letter-suffixed districts (U022A), several prefixes beyond the obvious ones (IS, VC, J, HE), and bare numerics. Constraining it to the tidy shape would reject real records. Values that merely look WRONG rather than unexpected -- placeholder and test records -- are caught by the sync, which warns and skips them.

citation.description: A pointer to the authority for a value. Every statutory parameter carries one. Citations are data to be verified against current statute text, not facts to be trusted from memory -- this area of Vermont law has been amended every session since 2022.

session_law.description: The act that set or last amended this value, where applicable.

quote.description: The operative sentence from the statute, quoted verbatim. Makes a citation checkable without leaving the page.

verified.description: True only when a human has read the current statute text and confirmed this value. The engine refuses to produce a number from an unverified parameter -- it returns null and marks the computation node unverified, so an unverified parameter can never silently become a published figure.
